PM Narendra Modi inaugurates COSMOS (Cosmology Education and Research Training Centre) LED Dome Planetarium in Mysuru on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
P rime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Bengaluru on Friday (November 13, 2026) to take part in a series of events, including the launch of the Pink Line Metro, the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat Express and the inauguration of four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.
He arrived at HAL Airport, where he was received by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Governor Sudha Yadav, Union Minister of State for Railways V. Somanna and Bengaluru MP Shobha Karandlaje. He then proceed to S-VYASA university to participate in golden jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram.

According to an official statement, he will flag off the services on the new metro line and take a ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station, lay the foundation stone, inaugurate various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru and address the gathering.

The programme will also commemorate the birth centenary of former RSS general secretary, H V Sheshadri.
The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. India has seen many great astronomers, such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya and Nilakantha Somayaji. The advanced instruments and technology we have today did not exist back then. Despite this, they made major discoveries and carried out difficult calculations, said PM Modi after inaugurating the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru.
The facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels and 4.2 crore individual LEDs. It includes a Sky Theatre, exhibition halls, an astronomy museum and training facilities, with the aim of promoting astronomy education and public outreach.
As India achieves one scientific breakthrough after another, Mysuru is also adding a new chapter to India’s scientific journey with this state-of-the-art COSMOS Planetarium, he added.
Our government opened up the space sector. This has created new opportunities for the private sector. India’s startups have also been given an opportunity to showcase their potential.
Underscoring Karnataka’s contribution to India’s space programme, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the country’s space journey was incomplete without the State’s contributions, from Aryabhata, India’s first satellite, to Chandrayaan, Aditya-L1 and the ambitious Gaganyaan mission.
Recalling the contributions of the Mysore Maharajas to scientific development, the CM cited their vision that had resulted in the establishment of top institutions including the IISc.
Karnataka government is ready to support the Centre in establishment of new centres of excellence. We are ready to support and encourage young minds and develop skills to our engineering graduates, Mr. Shivakumar said.
Seeking PM’s support in bringing the Mekedatu project to life, Mr. Shivakumar also reiterated the State’s concerns over the Kasturirangan Committee report on the ecologically sensitive areas of the Western Ghats.
Raising concerns over primary education and migration to urban centres, the Chief Minister said economic migration for education and employment was leading to a significant shift in population patterns.
To address this challenge, he requested the Ministry of Corporate Affairs to issue advisories aligning corporate CSR initiatives with Karnataka’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CCSR) Guidelines. This, he said, would help upgrade 1,000 government schools into Karnataka Public Schools and strengthen the public education system.
Developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) in partnership with the University of Mysore, the planetarium features a 15-metre-diameter tilted LED dome with seating capacity for around 160 people. It is developed on the foothills of Chamundi. Mr Modi will be addressing a gathering after the inauguration.
The planetarium will initially screen a specially produced 12-minute introductory show, ‘Our Home, Our Cosmos’, which explores Mysuru’s cultural heritage and its historical connections with scientific inquiry and astronomy. Produced in English, Kannada and Hindi, the show will be followed by two licensed productions, ‘Cosmos Odyssey’ and ‘Voyager’.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrives in Mysuru to inaugurate COSMOS Mysuru LED Dome Planetarium. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and other dignitaries were present at the helipad.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to increase the Centre’s financial contribution towards Metro projects, expedite pending approvals and address the state’s concerns over drought relief, sugarcane prices and the Kasturirangan Report concerning the Western Ghats.
In a memorandum submitted to Mr. Modi on November 13, Mr Shivakumar said Karnataka bears more than 80% of the financial burden of Metro projects despite the stipulated 50:50 partnership between the Centre and state. He sought a share of operational losses, foreign exchange risks on external loans and faster project clearances.
The Chief Minister also sought urgent approval for Bengaluru Metro’s proposed Red Line (Phase 3A) connecting Sarjapur and Hebbal. He further requested permission to construct double-decker infrastructure along Metro corridors wherever technically feasible, with Karnataka willing to bear the additional cost.
On drought relief, he said 226 of Karnataka’s 240 taluks had been declared drought-affected, with nearly 58 lakh hectares of crops damaged and estimated losses of ₹62,482 crore. He sought early release of ₹22,400.58 crore in NDRF assistance.
Mr Shivakumar also urged the Centre to address sugarcane farmers’ pricing demands and reconsider the Kasturirangan Report notification identifying 20,668 sq km across 1,449 villages in 10 Karnataka districts as Ecologically Sensitive Areas.
After concluding his speech and inaugurating the Bengaluru Metro Pink Line and several development projects in the city, Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for Mysuru.
There, he is scheduled to inaugurate COSMOS (Cosmology Education and Research Training Centre), the Mysuru Planetarium located at the foothills of Chamundi Hill, and launch a sapling plantation drive for the Bharat Vana Miyawaki mini-forest project at K.C. Layout Park.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted three energy projects in Karnataka, including an expanded LPG bottling plant, a marketing terminal and a Compressed Biogas (CBG) plant in Bengaluru, as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s energy security.
Mr. Modi said the crore compressed biogas (CBG) plant at the Karnataka Compost Development Corporation (KCDC) premises in Bengaluru would produce around 13 tonnes of biogas daily, improving waste management and reducing expenditure on natural gas imports.
Highlighting India’s clean energy initiatives, Mr. Modi said the country’s renewable energy capacity had crossed 300 GW. He also noted that over 40,000 households in Karnataka had installed rooftop solar systems under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, receiving assistance of around ₹80,000 per household.
Under the PM-KUSUM scheme, more than eight lakh solar pumps were being used to support irrigation in Karnataka, he said.
More than 60 railway stations in Karnataka have been selected for redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station scheme, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said.
He cited Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subramanya among the stations being upgraded.
He said the redevelopment would combine modern infrastructure with passenger-friendly facilities, including provisions for senior citizens and persons with disabilities. The initiative aims to bring facilities traditionally associated with airports to railway stations, making improved travel amenities accessible to poor and middle-class families.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi drew a comparison between India’s growing number of chess Grandmasters and Bengaluru Metro’s expansion, directly addressing Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar during his speech.
“We are continuously scoring centuries. DK Shivakumar ji, I was mentioning this because you may have heard a few days ago that India scored a century in Grandmaster chess. India now has 100 chess Grandmasters,” Mr Modi said.
He further said that Namma Metro, which had a network of just 17 km in 2014, had expanded to more than 100 km. Bengaluru has become the third city, after the Delhi-NCR and Mumbai Metropolitan regions, to cross the 100-km mark in its Metro network.
Describing Bengaluru as India’s Silicon Valley and a major engine of innovation and economic growth, Mr Modi said the Centre was prioritising the region’s development and modern public infrastructure. He added that Metro expansion reflected the government’s commitment to improving ease of living and travel, particularly for middle-class families.
A few days after Karnataka received its first Vande Bharat Sleeper train, the state had received another Vande Bharat service connecting it with Goa, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said.
Mr. Modi said the new train would offer passengers across Karnataka, including Bengaluru and the coastal region, a semi-high-speed travel experience.
Highlighting the expansion of railway infrastructure, he said Karnataka’s railway budget had increased ninefold over the past decade. He also announced four additional Amrit Bharat Stations and two projects involving railway track doubling and electrification in the state.
Prime Minister Modi paid tribute to former Union Minister and Bengaluru South MP Ananth Kumar, recalling his close association with the region.
Noting that Thursday marked Kumar’s death anniversary, Mr. Modi said the late leader had a special attachment to Bengaluru. He added that witnessing the inauguration of the Pink Line of Namma Metro would have brought immense joy to Kumar.
Mr. Modi said that the newly inaugurated Pink Line of Bengaluru Metro would improve connectivity to educational institutions, including IIM Bengaluru, as well as major business, technology and commercial centres across the city.
Mr. Modi said the project would make commuting more convenient for millions of people while helping them save time and money.
He said the projects launched in Karnataka would strengthen Bengaluru’s identity as a technology city and accelerate the state’s contribution towards building a developed India. He also claimed that 500 million people had been lifted out of extreme poverty in recent years.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said infrastructure development and improved connectivity play a crucial role in the country’s economic growth, creating new opportunities for employment, industry and progress.
Addressing the event in Bengaluru after the inauguration of the pink line metro and other initiatives, Mr. Modi said that better connectivity enables development opportunities to reach every section of society, thereby strengthening the fight against poverty.
He said nearly 50 crore citizens had emerged from extreme poverty in recent years, attributing this progress to expanding development opportunities.
D.K. Shivakumar submitted a representation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking a fair deal for Karnataka across various sectors. Thanking the Prime Minister for his support, Mr. Shivakumar said the State expected equitable consideration for all sections of society.
Chief Minister Shivakumar urged PM Modi to intervene in addressing the concerns of sugarcane farmers in Karnataka, who are demanding ₹5,500 per tonne against the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of ₹3,650.
Mr. Shivakumar said sugarcane farmers were facing difficulties and highlighted that the sugar minimum selling price (MSP) had remained unchanged at ₹31 per kg since 2019. He also sought a fair share of ethanol allocation for Karnataka, urging the Centre to address the issues affecting the State’s sugar sector.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to provide financial assistance to Karnataka to address severe drought conditions and crop losses across the State.
Mr. Shivakumar said, “Karnataka had received its second-lowest rainfall in 70 years, with 246 of the state’s 240 taluks declared drought-affected. Nearly 85 lakh hectares of crops had suffered damage, and I seek ₹22,000 crore in assistance under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).
He also offered to lead an all-party delegation to meet the Prime Minister to discuss farmers’ concerns, including sugarcane prices and ethanol allocation.
Amid a political dispute between the ruling Congress in Karnataka and the BJP regarding cost sharing over the Bengaluru metro, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to ensure fairer financial sharing for Bengaluru Metro projects and expedite pending approvals for expansion.
Mr. Shivakumar said “Karnataka bears a higher financial burden despite the proposed 50:50 Centre-state partnership, including land acquisition costs, state taxes and loan repayments.
Highlighting delays in project clearances, he said that the proposed Red Line had been pending for two years and urged the Centre to expedite approvals. He also called for project costs to reflect the actual conditions of individual cities rather than a uniform national average.
He urged Mr. Modi to extend the Centre’s financial support to Bengaluru Metro by sharing operational cash losses and foreign exchange risks on external loans.
He also proposed establishing a dedicated technical institution for Metro projects across India to streamline approvals and promote indigenous technology. Referring to Bengaluru’s ambition of expanding its Metro network to 500 km, Mr. Shivakumar said the expansion could help address 50% of the city’s traffic problem with the Centre’s support.
Karnataka reveals it is funding 84% of Bengaluru Metro costs and seeks greater Centre funding and faster clearances for Phase 3 and future lines.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar sought Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s support for Karnataka’s development, highlighting Bengaluru’s contribution to the national economy and its growing prominence in technology, defence and space sectors.
Speaking at the inauguration of the Bengaluru Metro Pink Line, Mr Shivakumar said Karnataka ranked first in exports and talent, second in GST collections and had recorded the highest FDI inflows over the past five years.
“We want your help,” he told the Prime Minister, emphasising the state’s contribution to India’s growth. He also highlighted Bengaluru Metro’s expansion, stating that over 103 km of the network had been completed, with plans to expand it to at least 500 km to ease traffic congestion.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar highlighted Karnataka’s legacy of pioneering achievements, describing Bengaluru as a city that has consistently been at the forefront of India’s development.
Speaking at event at IIM Bangalore, he recalled that Asia’s first hydroelectric power station was established at Shivanasamudra in Karnataka in 1902, making Bengaluru one of the first Indian cities to receive electricity. He also highlighted the establishment of India’s first aircraft manufacturing facility at HAL, the first global R&D centre of Texas Instruments and the country’s first iPhone assembly facility in Bengaluru. He said these milestones reflected Karnataka’s strong industrial and technological foundation.
​ Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express: PM Modi to flag off new service The Yeshwantpur-Mangaluru-Madgaon-Yeshwantpur Vande Bharat Express will be flagged off on November 13.
The Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express will be launched on November 13, 2026, from Bengaluru and Mangaluru Junctions simultaneously. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will flag off the service from Bengaluru, while Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will do it from the Mangaluru junction.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda briefed Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the Pink Line Metro’s route and connectivity following its inauguration in Bengaluru on Friday.
According to an official statement from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the two leaders explained the Metro route using a model map displayed at the station.
Mr. Shivakumar also briefed Modi on the benefits of implementing the double-decker model in Bengaluru and its potential to ease traffic congestion in the city.
Mr. Modi arrived at the IIM-Bangalore auditorium after taking a ride on Bengaluru’s Pink Line Metro. On his arrival at the auditorium, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar presented Mr. Modi with a statue of Bengaluru founder Nadaprabhu Kempegowda.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the elevated section of Bengaluru’s Pink Line Metro at S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, in the presence of Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.
The Pink Line is part of Namma Metro’s Phase II and is designed to connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in north Bengaluru. The 21.25-km corridor comprises a 7.5-km elevated section and a 13.76-km underground section.
Once fully operational, the corridor is projected to carry approximately 3.76 lakh passengers daily, according to the Detailed Project Report (DPR).
Mr. Modi later travelled by Metro to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station accompanied by Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya.
Before entering the platform, Mr Modi purchased a Metro ticket. BMRCL officials briefed him on the project before he boarded the train, a BMRCL source told The Hindu.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav have arrived by helicopter at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Training Centre campus near Dairy Circle on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru.
Modi will proceed to S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, where he, along with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, will flag off the Pink Line Metro service and undertake a ride to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.
The PM will also unveil plaques marking the foundation stone-laying of three projects, including a compressed biogas plant at Haralakunte village in Bengaluru South and two power transmission projects.
He will also inaugurate renewable energy transmission schemes in Koppal, Gadag and Bidar.
The programme also includes dedication of an 80 TMT LPG cavern developed by HPCL, the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of MRPL, railway doubling and electrification projects.
Mr Modi will virtually flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express before delivering his address from 1.35 p.m to 2.15 p.m. He is scheduled to depart at 2.15 p.m.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to arrive by helicopter at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Training Centre campus, near Dairy Circle on Bannerghatta Road, at around 12.30 p.m.
From there, he will proceed to S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, where he, along with Karnataka Chief Minister D. K Shivakumar will flag off the Pink Line Metro service and undertake a ride to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.
The inauguration marks the opening of the 7.5-km elevated section of the Pink Line, stretching from Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya. However, commercial operations on the newly inaugurated stretch will commence on November 14, according to Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL).
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who is in Bengaluru to inaugurate the elevated stretch of the city’s Pink Line Metro, has left for S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station after attending the Golden Jubilee celebrations of S-VYASA University’s Prashanti Kutiram and the birth centenary celebrations of former RSS General Secretary H.V. Sheshadri.
He is scheduled to flag off the Metro service and undertake a ride from S.G. Palya station to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.
PM Modi said the government’s effort was to take the benefits of Ayurveda and yoga to every citizen. With holistic healthcare becoming a new movement across the world, there was also growing interest in Ayurveda and naturopathy.
For the first time since Independence, a separate Ministry of Ayush had been created in the country he said. Mr. Modi said exports of Ayush products were also increasing and that the economy associated with the Ayush sector had grown to several lakh crore rupees. He said with turmeric seeing growing demand across the world, the government had also set up the National Turmeric Board to boost production, quality and exports.
Modi said that 140 crore Indians were working towards the shared goal of building a Viksit Bharat and a recent World Bank report had provided fresh impetus to this effort noting that nearly 50 crore Indians had come out of “extreme poverty” over the past 12 to 13 years.
The effort should be to make a healthy lifestyle a priority for every family, and yoga could play a major role in this. He said he always maintained that yoga brought rog mukti (freedom from disease) as well as bhog mukti (freedom from material indulgence).
Yoga was the biggest health gift that came at zero cost, he said, urging S-VYASA university to prepare a roadmap for the next 25 years, with a focus on contributing to Viksit Bharat.
PM said that when India was caught in the chains of slavery, lakhs of freedom fighters were fighting for independence, while national spiritual leaders such as Swami Vivekananda were awakening India’s spiritual consciousness and showing the country’s youth the path of yoga.
He said the inspiration from sages such as Swami Vivekananda had led to the establishment of institutions such as Prashanti Kutiram. The institution had not only worked to take yoga to people but had also conducted research to test it against modern scientific standards.
Mr. Modi said, in the last 12 years, India had presented its culture, identity and knowledge and science before the world with full confidence. As a result of this, the entire world now celebrates International Yoga Day.
The PM said that on International Yoga Day, yoga-related programmes are held across the world, from Australia to Africa and America, with crores of people taking part. He said yoga had now reached schools, institutions and workplaces in many countries. In Saudi Arabia, he said, yoga had been recognised as a sporting activity and its Sports Ministry had signed an agreement with India’s Ministry of Ayush to promote it.
Modi said that whenever he travelled abroad, yoga almost always came up in conversations during lunches or dinners with foreign guests and heads of State. He said that in the families of several prominent world leaders, there was someone or the other associated with yoga. This showed how far India had reached through yoga. Yoga had become a gateway for the world to know India.
He said he had seen foreign nationals such as members of Qatar’s royal family, who were deeply devoted to yoga. He added that India had also honoured several such people with the Padma Shri.
PM Narendra Modi paid his respects to H.V. Sheshadri on his birth centenary, saying that he had devoted his entire life to the mission of vyakti nirman se rashtra nirman (nation-building through individual development). He said Mr. Sheshadri understood that for the country to reach the heights of success, it needed “dedicated, capable and disciplined” citizens.
He said Mr. Sheshadri devoted himself entirely to preparing such citizens. The goals he pursued while working in the RSS continue to inspire crores of swayamsevaks even today.
PM Modi said that whenever people remembered H.V. Sheshadri, the first thing that came to mind was his simple nature. Despite his stature and vast experience, he was humble in his behaviour. He believed in staying behind and bringing others forward, bringing people together and preparing them for the country. This was a major part of his life’s work.
He said Mr. Sheshadri often gave the example of a mother, who stays awake the whole night to care for her child, looks after the child and works without any selfish motive. If the same feeling was extended to society it could benefit society greatly. Sheshadri remained devoted to serving society with the same selflessness as a mother.
Modi said he had received H.V. Sheshadri’s affection and guidance over the years, and that the memories of the time spent with him and his words remained precious to him.
Recalling one of his sayings, Mr. Modi said Sheshadri would often say that if one gave to society with both hands, society returned it with lakhs of hands. He said he had seen this come true repeatedly in his own life. While serving the people, he had always received their blessings, which is one of his biggest assets
PM Narendra Modi said he was getting the opportunity to experience the wonderful energy of yoga in Bengaluru. He said Karnataka had been a centre of yoga for centuries, and several yoga teachers and scholars had been born here and enriched the tradition.
He also cited Kannada cinema legend Dr. Rajkumar as an example of personalities who had contributed to yoga alongside their work in the world of art.
The 50-year journey of SVYASA Prashanti Kutiram was a story of service and dedication that every Indian should know. He said the way a simple yoga centre had grown into such a large movement was an inspiration in itself.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi digitally laid the foundation stone for the Golden Jubilee Administrative Block of S-VYASA University and digitally inaugurated the university’s Thiruvananthapuram off-campus.
He also released six books authored by H.V. Sheshadri, whose works in Kannada have been translated into Hindi and English, as part of his birth centenary celebrations.
The event has brought together two occasions, says RSS General Secretary Dattatreya Hosabale - the golden jubilee celebrations of S-VYASA University’s Prashanti Kutiram and the birth centenary of former RSS General Secretary H.V. Sheshadri, who had been a source of guidance to swayamsevaks like him.
He said that countless people, including himself, had been associated with H.V. Sheshadri over the years. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, too, had been closely acquainted with Mr. Sheshadri.
Mr. Hosabale said Mr. Sheshadri, after completing his M.Sc., worked as a teacher for a short period before dedicating himself to nation-building through the RSS, where he became a swayamsevak (volunteer).
As an RSS swayamsevak and later a pracharak (full-time worker), Mr. Sheshadri held various responsibilities. He also served as the RSS Sarkaryavah (General Secretary) for 13 years, Mr. Hosabale said.
Mr. Sheshadri, he added, believed that yoga should not be viewed only in terms of an individual’s physical and mental health. He saw yoga from India’s perspective as something that could benefit all of humanity. He believed that the different dimensions of yoga could play a significant role in guiding humankind in the future, especially at a time when people were experiencing stress due to modern life.
Years ago, Mr. Sheshadri had written a small book on yoga, which he had also spoken about at the S-VYASA campus, where he stayed for a long time. His interest was not limited to the benefits of yoga for one’s own health or personal practice. He would speak to people visiting the campus about how yoga should become a part of their lives and how, through a yogic way of life, they could make their lives meaningful.
He explained in different ways and from different perspectives how a yogic way of life could contribute to nation-building, service, social transformation and the progress of others, MR. Hosabale reminisced.

Charging fares inflating the distance by 40% on Konkan Railway network between Thokur and Madgaon and 100% on 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat section the reason for extra fares.
The SWR justified the inflated distance saying the Indian Railways follows the practice on almost all Ghat routes because of the challenges in operating through difficult terrains. KRCL was initially allowed to inflate the distance to recover the construction cost of about ₹3,555 crore. The Corporation now justifies the additional collection due to “heavy maintenance cost (due to difficult geographical conditions).”
